A comprehensive overview of quadratic equations, including quadratic trinomials, completing the square,
    the discriminant, Vieta’s formulas, factoring, real-life applications, and even methods for solving them mentally.
Before solving quadratic equations, you must be able to solve elementary ones. There is no other way. Don't even try.
Huge collection of word problems which lead to an equations with detailed solutions.
An open and free online collection of mathematics educational materials.
A large amount of materials and many typical practice problems.

Learn how quadratic equations arise from real-life situations,
    what quadratic equations and quadratic trinomials are,
    how they are related, and how to determine whether an equation is quadratic.

Examples of various real-life situations that boil down to quadratic equations.
          This will make it clear why we need to be able to solve them at all.

Polynomial with the maximum power of the variable equal to two.
          Acts as a "template" or "general form" for all quadratic equations.
Any equation that can be reduced to the form of a quadratic trinomial by transformations without losing roots.

Quadratic equations with missing terms (incomplete quadratics) are the simplest forms of quadratic equations where the coefficient B, C, or both are missing.
    Let's learn how to solve them correctly in each specific case.
What is an incomplete quadratic equation?
A quadratic equation in which coefficient B or C or both are zero.
How to solve incomplete quadratic equations?
Detailed analysis of solving all types of incomplete quadratic equations with derivation of general formulas.
General formulas for incomplete quadratic equations
General formulas for solving incomplete quadratic equations

Formulas for all three types of incomplete quadratic equations:
          when "B" and "C" are zero, when "C" is zero, and when "B" is zero.
